title: BA2/391/2023 of VICTOR JEROME Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Second Bail Application No. 391 of 2023
Victor Jerome ........Applicant

Present:-
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Pramod Tiwari, Brief Holder for the State.

Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Applicant Victor Jerome is in judicial custody
in FIR No.0051 of 2021, under Sections 419, 420, 467,
468, 471, 120-B IPC, Police Station Ghansali, District
Tehri Garhwal. He has sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. This is the second bail application. The first
bail application, being BA1 No.458 of 2023, was
dismissed as withdrawn on 21.11.2023.
4. It is a case of online fraud. The informant was
cheated in the name of providing him some financial
assistance. The FIR records that huge money was
deposited by the informant in various accounts.

2
5. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that the applicant has no role in the case; the
applicant was not seen withdrawing the money; his wife
was allegedly found withdrawing the money; the recovery
is joint from the applicant and his wife, who is co-accused, and only one such phone number was
recovered, which was used in the crime. Therefore, it is a
case for bail.
6. Learned State Counsel would submit that the
informant was telephonically cheated and required to
deposit money, and four telephone numbers, recovered
from the applicant, were found to have been used for
calling the informant. The IMEI numbers have been
detailed in the counter affidavit. It is also argued that co-accused, who is the wife of the applicant, has been seen
in the CCTV footage withdrawing the money, when the
applicant was along with her.
7. It is a stage of bail. Much of the discussion is
not expected of. Arguments are being appreciated with the
caveat that any observation made in this order shall have
no bearing at any subsequent stage of the trial, or in any
other proceeding.

3
8. It is a case of online fraud. These are faceless
crime. The applicant is a citizen of Nigeria. Four of the
phones that have been used in the commission of crime,
were recovered from his possession. His wife was seen
withdrawing the money in the CCTV footages, when the
applicant was also with her. They both were arrested
together.
9. Having considered the nature of offence, its
ramification and consequences in the society, this Court
does not see any reason, which may entitle the applicant
to bail. Accordingly, the bail application deserves to be
rejected.
10. The bail application is rejected.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 27.02.2024
Ravi Bisht
